# Fort Worth Botanic Garden - Digital

> Home for a growing collection of digital tools and resources from the Fort Worth Botanic
> Garden (FWBG) and the Botanical Research Institute of Texas (BRIT), including datasets,
> dashboards, and applications. Content is aggregated onto this site (fwbg.github.io) from
> several source repositories via automated and manual publishing.

This site mixes hand-maintained scaffolding with pages auto-published from sibling repos. Treat
`begonias/`, its variants (`begonias-embed/`, `begonias-unbranded/`, `begonias-unbranded-plain/`), and
and `collections/` as generated mirrors, not editable sources — their source repos are linked below.

## About FWBG and BRIT

The Fort Worth Botanic Garden (FWBG), founded in 1934, is Texas's oldest major botanic garden:
110 acres in Fort Worth's Cultural District. The Botanical Research Institute of Texas (BRIT),
founded in 1987, is a botanical research institution with a herbarium of about 1.5 million
specimens, a library, laboratories, a seed bank, and a publishing division. In 2020 the two
merged into a single nonprofit. The City of Fort Worth still owns most of the Garden's land and
buildings, and the combined organization manages the Garden. FWBG and BRIT are the same
organization, so content on this site may carry either name — FWBG generally refers to the
garden and its living collections, and BRIT refers to the research side, including the
herbarium, library, and preserved collections.

This site (fwbg.github.io) is a separate, digital-tools-and-data site — for the organization's
own website (visiting, programs, general information), see [fwbg.org](https://fwbg.org).

## Pages

- [Home](https://fwbg.github.io/index.html): Landing page with links to FWBG and BRIT GitHub organizations.
- [Home (minimal variant)](https://fwbg.github.io/index-minimal.html): Plain-styled alternate homepage with the same purpose and links, using its own stylesheet.
- [Begonia Collection dashboard](https://fwbg.github.io/begonias/index.html): Interactive React dashboard exploring the Begonia collection (charts, sortable table). Auto-published from [FWBG/living_collections](https://github.com/FWBG/living_collections).
- Begonia dashboard variants (same dashboard and data, different presentation; all auto-published from the same repo):
  - [Embed](https://fwbg.github.io/begonias-embed/index.html): Branded, built to sit in an iframe on fwbg.org; reports its height to the parent page.
  - [Unbranded](https://fwbg.github.io/begonias-unbranded/index.html): Neutral styling without FWBG brand tokens.
  - [Unbranded, plain masthead](https://fwbg.github.io/begonias-unbranded-plain/index.html): Unbranded with a plain masthead.
- [FWBG Collections](https://fwbg.github.io/collections/index.html): Index of Fort Worth Botanic Garden and BRIT digital collections (living collections; plant, fungal and lichen herbarium portals; library and archives; Carlquist collections; Zenodo community). Auto-published from [FWBG/collections](https://github.com/FWBG/collections).

## Source repositories

- [FWBG/FWBG.github.io](https://github.com/FWBG/FWBG.github.io): This site itself (publish target; also hosts the manually-maintained homepage).
- [FWBG/living_collections](https://github.com/FWBG/living_collections): Source for the Begonia dashboard published to `/begonias/` and its variant folders.
- [FWBG/collections](https://github.com/FWBG/collections): Source for the collections index published to `/collections/`.
- [FWBG on GitHub](https://github.com/FWBG): Full list of FWBG repositories.
- [BRIT on GitHub](https://github.com/BRITorg/): Full list of Botanical Research Institute of Texas repositories.

## Optional

- [PUBLISHING.md](https://fwbg.github.io/PUBLISHING.md): Detailed explanation of the three mechanisms that feed content into this site.
- [llms-full.txt](https://fwbg.github.io/llms-full.txt): Includes "External collection portals — crawling guidance" — before crawling a Symbiota herbarium link, UNT Portal to Texas History link, or other third-party collection system linked from the Collections page, check there for a bulk-data endpoint (e.g. Darwin Core Archive) instead of paging through search results.
